entries.en: Added a country-by-country guide to customs duty, with the UK's tariff rates for figures, cards, consoles and books, and the EU's new €3 flat duty.
Added a guide to buying from Suruga-ya, Mandarake, Lashinbang, Toranoana and Melonbooks, including which of them ship abroad themselves.
Added a guide to lost or damaged parcels: which services pay out themselves, which pass claims to Japan Post, and the deadlines for claiming.
Added a guide to reading Mercari and Yahoo! Auctions listings, using the marketplaces' own definitions of condition grades and bidding.
Added perfume, skincare and make-up, over-the-counter medicine, and plants and seeds to the items checked against each service's prohibited list.
Read FROM JAPAN's full prohibited list. Its rules for replica guns, swords, lithium batteries and food, previously marked as not stated, are now taken from it.
Added an estimate of US customs duty by type of item, following the 12.5% rate on goods made in Japan in force since 24 July 2026. It is shown next to the totals, not added to them.
Added Doorzo as a fifth service, with its fees taken from its own user guide. Its payment fee is not published and is counted as ¥0, which is noted wherever it comes out cheapest.
Totals now show an approximate figure in the destination's currency, at European Central Bank reference rates (Taiwan dollars at the US Federal Reserve's H.10 rate).
Added a glossary and a page of frequently asked questions.
Added Japan Post's airmail small packets, airmail parcels and surface parcels alongside EMS, with which services offer each.
Turned each country's import tax page into a full guide to buying from Japan for that country, and added eight guides by kind of item.
Redesigned the site and expanded every page with worked examples.
Merged pages that gave the same answer for every country into single pages.
Added shops in Japan that ship abroad themselves, shown where buying direct is possible.
Added Taiwan and Hong Kong as destinations.
Started checking each order against the services' prohibited-item rules and Japan Post's rules for each destination.
First version: fees for FROM JAPAN, Buyee, ZenMarket and Neokyo checked against each company's own pages.
